name: John Hickenlooper

issue_poll.name: Colorado Polling Institute statewide poll (New Bridge Strategies / Aspect Strategic), Mar 20-25, 2026, 613 likely voters
issue_poll.note: No fall 2026 Colorado poll with an issue ranking was found (Keating Research Nov 1-2 poll had horse race only). Ranks 1-5 from the same poll's open-ended top priority question (cost of living 9%, housing 7%, taxes 7%, immigration 6%, homelessness 6%; reported at https://www.cpr.org/2026/04/08/colorado-voters-pessimistic-new-poll/). Ranks 6-10 added from the same poll's share calling each a problem: utility costs 93% / gas 89% (merged as energy prices), health care costs over 90%, wildfire risk about 90%, low snowfall/water 84%, good-paying jobs 75%. Groceries and home/car insurance folded into cost of living. Question was framed around state government priorities; national and state issues ranked together.

issues.detail: End Trump tariffs; end the Iran war; expand Medicare drug price negotiation from 10 to 20 drugs.
Enforce ROAD to Housing Act limits on large investors buying homes (already law); add incentives to increase housing supply.
Permanently extend tax breaks on tips and overtime; undo 2025 reconciliation law cuts if Democrats win Congress.

Replace ICE with a separate border-security agency; require ICE agents unmasked with body cameras; bar raids at schools, hospitals, polling places; citizenship path for DREAMers, TPS holders, essential workers.
Restore federal EV incentives; expand wind and solar; end the Iran war to lower gas prices.
Create a public option; restore Medicaid and ACA cuts; Medicare negotiates all drug prices; require hospital and insurer price disclosure before care.
Reduce wildfire risk and protect forests, working with Republicans.
Pass his snowpack monitoring bill and Water Project Navigators Act; fund water conservation projects.
Raise federal minimum wage in stages, starting at $15/hour.

plan_caveats: Issue poll is from March 2026 and asked about state-government priorities; ranks 6-10 come from 'is this a problem' shares, not a single ranked question.
Campaign issues page (hickenlooper.com/issues) could not be fetched; positions come from 2026 news Q&As and voter guides (Colorado Sun, CPR, Summit Daily, Colorado Politics).
Hickenlooper declined the Colorado Newsline questionnaire; most specifics come from the June 2026 primary rather than the general election.
Drug negotiation stated two ways: expand from 10 to 20 drugs (CPR) and let Medicare negotiate all drug prices (Summit Daily); both recorded.
Housing rated Partial because the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act he campaigned on became law in July 2026 without Trump's signature.
Water bills named in the Q&A as legislation he is leading; exact snowpack bill title not given in the campaign source (it is the Hickenlooper-Curtis snowpack monitoring bill).
Considering a moratorium on new federal oil and gas leases was not counted as a commitment.
